subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw standardize a persisted `ui.accessibility.plainText` contract, and what ASCII vocabulary should it use for tools, status indicators, selectors, and separators?
rationale: The problem is established, but repository policy sets a high bar for new config and the choice determines a lasting user-visible presentation contract across OpenClaw and pi-tui-owned rendering.

options.title: Persisted plain-text mode
options.body: Add `ui.accessibility.plainText`, use explicit ASCII forms such as `[ok]`, `[err]`, `>`, and `-`, and cover all TUI presentation paths consistently.

options.title: Runtime-only flag
options.body: Add an `openclaw tui --plain` flag without persistent config, reducing config surface but requiring accessibility users to remember the flag on every launch.

options.title: Wait for upstream defaults
options.body: Defer the feature until pi-tui provides a complete accessibility theme, leaving OpenClaw-owned emoji and glyph output unchanged meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Persisted plain-text mode
recommendation.body: Add `ui.accessibility.plainText`, use explicit ASCII forms such as `[ok]`, `[err]`, `>`, and `-`, and cover all TUI presentation paths consistently.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository explicitly routes TUI ownership to this person, making them the strongest available owner for the presentation and activation contract.
